title: POC Weekly Security Sync - Crestmore Bank
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 summary and architecture diagram (link in notes)
Customer to provide SAML metadata and IdP test tenant by 2026-06-05
SE to run audit-log export test and share sample by 2026-06-07
Schedule on-prem network review with Crestmore networking team week of 2026-06-08
action_items: Ethan Park: validate SSO SAML metadata in staging; due 2026-06-05
Maya Chen: share SOC2 Artifact Summary and encryption docs; due 2026-06-04
Rajiv Patel (Crestmore): provide IdP SAML metadata + test creds; due 2026-06-05

summary: Weekly pilot security sync focused on SSO/SAML integration, audit log export/retention, SOC2 artifacts, and key management for the Crestmore Bank POC. SE demonstrated log export and retention controls; customer requested SOC2 summary and an on-prem networking review. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, we're on for the weekly security sync for the Crestmore POC.
[00:08] Laura Benson: Hi Maya, hi Ethan, thanks. We've got Laura, Marcus, Anita and Rajiv from our side. Good to see you both.
[00:15] Ethan Park: Morning all. Quick agenda - SSO status, audit log shipping + retention, SOC2 docs, KMS questions and any network/VPC items. Sound good?
[00:25] Marcus Lee: Yep, that's perfect. We had a blocker on SAML metadata last week so we'd like to resolve that.
[00:30] Anita Shah: Also want to confirm what logs we can pull for our SIEM and how retention works in the hosted POC tenant.
[00:38] Maya Chen: Great. Ethan, can you start with SSO?

[00:42] Ethan Park: Sure. So we added the SP metadata to your IdP on our staging tenant, we tested a couple of flows - login, token exchange - and saw a successful SAML assertion. There was a mismatch on the audience URL originally, that's fixed now.
[00:59] Rajiv Patel: I saw a failure earlier when our IdP returned an unexpected NameID format, is that something you support?
[01:05] Ethan Park: We support email and persistent NameIDs; if you've got transient we can map it but need the SAML metadata. Laura, did you push the updated metadata after the change?
[01:15] Laura Benson: We uploaded an export this morning but I wasn't sure if the cert rotated and if that would break anything. I'll confirm and re-export if needed.
[01:24] Ethan Park: Ok please send the metadata file to the shared secure S3 link. We'll validate in staging and let you know, should be quick once we have it.
[01:35] Maya Chen: Note: we asked for IdP test creds in the last email thread, if you can share those that accelerates it.
[01:42] Marcus Lee: We'll do that. Next, audit logs - Anita do you want to state your requirements?

[01:50] Anita Shah: We need all user auth events, API calls, model inference requests metadata (timestamp, model id, token counts) and admin actions. Retention must be at least 90 days hot and cold archive for 7 years for compliance.

[02:05] Ethan Park: For the hosted POC tenant we export logs into a shipping endpoint - we can push JSON lines to your SIEM or to an S3 bucket. Retention on our side is configurable; by default hosted keeps 30 days but for enterprise we can extend or set up automatic export to your archive.
[02:23] Laura Benson: We prefer near-real-time shipping to our Splunk instance, then cold archive to our S3 with encryption. How does Redwood handle log encryption and key management?

[02:33] Ethan Park: We support customer-managed keys via KMS for at-rest encryption on dedicated/private deployments. For hosted we use Redwood-managed KMS but can set up envelope encryption and support key wrapping if required. We can share the KMS architecture diagram in the notes.
[02:46] Rajiv Patel: For SOC2, do you have the list of controls and the latest report? We need the bridge letter and recent penetration test summary.

[02:53] Maya Chen: Yes, we have our SOC2 Type II report and additional artifacts. I'll share a trimmed Artifact Summary and the SOC2 summary doc after the call. Full reports will require an NDA but we'll follow the standard process.
[03:05] Marcus Lee: Timeline - we want to complete security gating for the pilot by mid-June so we can start performance tests the week of 2026-06-22. Is that feasible?
[03:14] Ethan Park: Feasible. Main dependencies are SAML test creds and confirmation of log shipping endpoint. Also network review if you choose VPC peering or on-prem option.
[03:22] Anita Shah: About VPC/on-prem - we want to see both configs. For now the hosted option is fine but we'd like to test a private deployment later in the POC.
[03:30] Ethan Park: Understood. We can spin up a private tenant for the network review. For hosted we can still do encrypted exports to your VPC via a connector.
[03:38] Laura Benson: One more question - can we limit access to model logs so only security ops can view content fields? We need RBAC for PII protection.
[03:45] Ethan Park: Yes, we have role-based permissions; you can mask or redact payloads at ingestion and control which roles have full view. We'll share the RBAC matrix in the doc pack.
[03:55] Rajiv Patel: Any limitations around audit log sampling or token-level detail? We need token usage by user to map cost and data lineage.
[04:02] Ethan Park: We capture token counts per request; for PII-sensitive fields we can configure redaction. Sampling can be disabled for the POC so you get full fidelity for the audit period.
[04:12] Maya Chen: Quick demo segment - Ethan can show the audit log export briefly and the retention setting in Console.

[04:20] Ethan Park: (screen share) Here is the Console - per-route logs, export configuration, and retention slider. You can select direct Splunk, S3, or syslog endpoint. Example export payload looks like this: timestamp, user_id, route, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, action.
[04:40] Anita Shah: I see. The export JSON keys are slightly different from our current parser; will we need an adaptor?
[04:46] Ethan Park: We can provide a mapping file and a small lambda to normalize keys, we'll include a sample transformer in the repo.
[04:55] Laura Benson: Great. SOC2 docs next - can you summarize the certification scope and date?

[05:01] Maya Chen: SOC2 Type II, scope covers hosting and platform controls for the hosted product; last audit ended March 2026. I'll attach the executive summary; full report requires a standard vendor access request which we'll coordinate.
[05:12] Marcus Lee: Any open exceptions or recent findings we should know about?
[05:16] Maya Chen: No current high severity exceptions; a couple of low-tier process items closed during remediation. We'll include the notes.
[05:24] Rajiv Patel: About PII - can you confirm encryption in transit and at rest for model inputs/outputs?

[05:30] Ethan Park: TLS in transit always; at rest encrypted with KMS. For hosted POC we can enable additional application-level encryption before persistence if you want to bring your own keys for wrapping.
[05:42] Anita Shah: If we use envelope encryption and customer-managed keys, how is key rotation handled?
[05:47] Ethan Park: KMS rotations are supported and we have processes for rewrapping. We'll share the key rotation playbook.
[05:55] Marcus Lee: Networking - what does the peering look like? Do you support private link / VPC peering and IP allowlisting?
[06:02] Ethan Park: Yes, support for VPC peering and PrivateLink in select regions; IP allowlisting for API is also supported for dedicated/private. For hosted we do allowlist + mutual TLS options.
[06:12] Laura Benson: Ok. On the SIEM side, can we get a sample payload from the export so our Splunk team can test ingestion?
[06:18] Ethan Park: I'll run a sample export this afternoon and drop the file in the shared bucket; Rajiv, can you confirm the target S3 path?
[06:24] Rajiv Patel: Will confirm after the call, but yes we'll provide path and creds.
[06:29] Anita Shah: One operational ask - can we disable auto-deletion of logs in hosted while the POC is active? We want to ensure nothing is purged until we've verified exports.
[06:36] Ethan Park: We can set retention to manual for the POC or schedule a hold; we'll put that in the action items.
[06:42] Maya Chen: Quick note on compliance - we also support audit trails for admin actions, and all changes are stamped with user and session id. That should cover your audit requirements.
[06:52] Laura Benson: Sounds good. Any performance tradeoffs we should be aware of if we enable full-fidelity logging and envelope encryption?
[06:59] Ethan Park: Minimal overhead for logging; envelope encryption adds CPU overhead on write but it's negligible for your expected workloads. We'll quantify in the performance test next week.
[07:09] Marcus Lee: Ok timeline recap please - Laura?
[07:12] Laura Benson: We'll provide SAML metadata + test creds by 2026-06-05, confirm Splunk S3 path by end of day 2026-06-04. We expect Redwood to send SOC2 summary by 2026-06-04.
[07:22] Maya Chen: Confirmed. We'll also run the audit-export sample and share artifacts by 2026-06-07. I'll schedule a network deep-dive with your net team for week of 2026-06-08.
[07:30] Rajiv Patel: One more - do you have a breach notification SLA? We need notification within 72 hours legally.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood has a 72-hour initial notification commitment and incident response playbook. We'll include that in the doc packet.
[07:45] Anita Shah: Anything else on RBAC? We want separation between platform admins and analyst roles.
[07:50] Ethan Park: We can provision role templates and a least-privilege setup; we'll include a recommended RBAC policy for your use case.
[07:58] Laura Benson: Perfect. Let's do the recap and close out.

[08:02] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send SOC2 summary and artifact notes, SE to run audit-export sample and share, customer to provide SAML metadata and IdP test creds, and schedule network review next week. Owners and due dates in the notes.
[08:15] Marcus Lee: Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnarounds.
[08:18] Maya Chen: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the doc pack and calendar invite for the network deep-dive. Bye.
[08:22] Meeting ended
